# 🔔 carillon [![Matrix](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-%23pimalaya-blue?style=flat&logo=matrix&logoColor=white)](https://matrix.to/#/#pimalaya:matrix.org) [![Mastodon](https://img.shields.io/badge/news-%40pimalaya-blue?style=flat&logo=mastodon&logoColor=white)](https://fosstodon.org/@pimalaya) [![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/sponsor-pink?style=flat&logo=github-sponsors&logoColor=white)](https://pimalaya.org/sponsor/)

CLI daemon that watches PIM accounts and fires local consumers on each change

> [!WARNING]
> This project is pre-release and unpublished. Its config and behaviour may change without notice until the first tagged version.

carillon is the lightweight frontend of [Carillon](https://github.com/pimalaya): a self-hostable daemon that holds a standing IMAP IDLE connection and, the instant a mailbox changes, fires a local consumer. It runs the whole watch on your machine, without the network-and-trust apparatus of a hosted service. It signals; it never syncs, and it never sees message content it does not fetch on your behalf.

## Features

- **Content-free watching**: holds IMAP IDLE and detects a change without reading message content, so nothing about your mail leaves your machine.
- **Enriched notifications**: on a change, resolve the new message locally (on the daemon's own connection) and pop a system notification naming the sender and subject — one per new message.
- **Shell hooks**: run any command on a change (e.g. kick a sync tool), with the raw event passed as environment variables, so a script can re-fetch or react however it likes.
- **Keyring-friendly credentials**: read the password or token from a command such as `pass` or `secret-tool`, never storing it in cleartext.
- **Multi-account config**: declare any number of accounts; pick which to watch with `-a <name>`.

## Installation

Pre-built binaries and package-manager recipes will land with the first release. For now, build from sources:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/pimalaya/carillon
```

## Configuration

A configuration is loaded from the first valid path among:

- the path passed with `-c <PATH>` or `CARILLON_CONFIG=<PATH>`
- $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/carillon/config.toml
- $HOME/.config/carillon/config.toml
- ./carillon.toml

The full field reference lives in [config.sample.toml](./config.sample.toml).

## Usage

Watch every configured account until interrupted, or name a subset:

```sh
carillon watch                # every configured account
carillon watch work personal  # just these two
```

Each account's watched mailbox comes from its own config (`mailbox`,
defaulting to INBOX).

Set `RUST_LOG=debug` for verbose logs. The complete command list is behind `carillon --help`.
